what: Made-up statements, one small set a sample. No session said any of this. They are here only so each drawing can show where the two marks would go: something said that never ran, and something that ran and was never said. A statement has the shape of today's grooph_plan call: so many subagents of a type. `before` and `seconds` place it that long before a real subagent's first start; `covers` are the real subagents it is taken to have meant; `unsaid` are real subagents the page marks as never said; `never` are subagents said and never seen.
